attempts.label: DANDI:001683
attempts.paper_title: Transcranial Focused Ultrasound Stimulation Targeting White Matter Inhibits Seizures in a Rat Model of Epilepsy
attempts.entry_title: White-matter tFUS against 4-AP seizures in rats (Gao et al. 2026)
attempts.summary: The paper's main seizure-suppression findings held: after tFUS, seizure count and percent time in seizure fell and inter-seizure interval rose, matching the reported percentages. Differences from sham held only in part, and the sham group was not steady, with seizure duration falling from about 50 s to 35 s. The EEG band-power and asymmetry-index findings were partly supported, and the epileptic phase-lag decrease was not specific to S1. The wild-type evoked-potential and gamma phase-lag findings could not be tested, since resting sham EEG is missing and the evoked-potential analysis is underspecified. Several verdicts assume a repeated-measures ANOVA, which the paper does not specify.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Gao, Frake, Durand and He (2026) on dandiset 001683, which holds the EEG and seizure labels of 16 rats with 4-AP seizures (10 given focused ultrasound to the corpus callosum, 6 sham) and the evoked-potential and EEG recordings of the wild-type phase of 23 rats. It compares seizure count, percent time in seizure, interval and duration between groups and time blocks, band power, the asymmetry index and the phase lag index, and the evoked potentials.

notebooks.title: Seizure metrics from the labels (Figs. 2 and 3)
Band power, asymmetry index and seizure PLI (Figs. 4, 6, S4, S5, S7)
Evoked potentials and PLI in wild-type rats (Fig. 5)

outcomes.statement: In the sham group, seizure durations from the ipsilateral and contralateral hemispheres do not differ significantly across time blocks or between hemispheres.
outcomes.quote: The Seizure Durations collected from both ipsilateral and contralateral hemispheres relative to the drug injection site were not significantly different across time or between hemispheres
outcomes.notes: The block effect on sham seizure duration is significant under every reading. Per seizure (1046 seizures) F = 30.45, p = 5.5e-24 ordinary and F = 37.48, p = 2.7e-29 repeated, with 12 and 13 of 25 Bonferroni post hoc comparisons significant; per rat p = 0.00145 ordinary (no post hoc comparison significant) and p = 0.00037 repeated (contralateral baseline against post 3, p = 0.026). The hemisphere effect is not significant (p = 0.16 to 0.63). Mean durations fall from 49.6 to 53.0 s at baseline to 34.8 to 35.7 s at post 3. Counting the seizures within 2 s of either end of a block as cut off (14 left out, against 6) gives block p = 0.0017 and 0.00043 per rat. The readings agree, so the outcome rests on none of them.
deviations: The seizure labels are the dandiset's own; their times are in minutes and are multiplied by 60 (checked against the EEG in eeg_blocks.ipynb).
Durations leave out the 6 seizures that start at a block's first sample (Methods C, "Seizures that either started before or continued after the recording were excluded").
BH635's five files are taken in time order (see fig2f-sham-percent-time-post3).

The repeated-measures reading of M3 is a linear mixed model with a random intercept per rat (REML), a standard stand-in for Prism's repeated-measures and mixed-effects analysis; its post hoc tests are t tests and its main effects F tests on Satterthwaite degrees of freedom, which on balanced data are those of the classical repeated-measures ANOVA.

outcomes.statement: Pooled over blocks, most seizures in the sham group last less than 2 minutes, and the two hemispheres have similar distributions.
outcomes.quote: The majority of recorded seizures lasted less than 2 minutes, and hemispheric distributions appear relatively similar
outcomes.notes: 99.4% of 527 ipsilateral and 99.2% of 521 contralateral sham seizures last under 120 s; medians 41.5 and 43.5 s; every rat 97% or more. KS D = 0.082, p = 0.056 (description only).
deviations: All seizures are counted, including the two that start at a block's first sample.

outcomes.statement: In the sham group, seizure count does not differ significantly between time blocks or hemispheres, with a slight decrease in the last two hours.
outcomes.quote: There were no significant differences in Seizure Count between time blocks or hemispheres; however, there was a slight decrease in number of seizures in the last two hours of the experiment
outcomes.notes: Block p = 0.97 (ordinary) and 0.82 (repeated), hemisphere p = 0.93 and 0.88, no post hoc comparison significant (smallest Bonferroni p = 1). Mean count 18.11 over baseline to post 1 and 16.50 over post 2 and post 3. With BH635's blocks by their labels the block effect stays non-significant (p = 0.66 and 0.61).
deviations: BH635's five files are taken in time order (see fig2f-sham-percent-time-post3); the label variant gives the same outcome.

outcomes.statement: In the sham group, percent time in seizure in the contralateral hemisphere differs significantly between the sham condition block and post 3, suggesting the model is no longer stable in the fifth hour.
outcomes.quote: percent time in seizure between sham and post 3 for the contralateral hemisphere was significantly different, which could mean that the seizure model is no longer stable during the fifth hour of the experiment
outcomes.notes: Under the repeated-measures reading, contralateral baseline (reading b of "sham") against post 3 is significant in its family, Bonferroni p = 0.040, a decrease from 25.6% to 15.5%; over all 25 comparisons it is not (p = 0.051). Condition against post 3 is not (p = 0.14). Under the ordinary reading no comparison is significant (p = 1). With BH635's files taken by their labels the comparison is not significant (p = 0.13 repeated, 0.94 ordinary).
deviations: Assumed that BH635's five files are the blocks baseline, condition, post 1, post 2 and post 3 in time order, though their labels read BASELINE, SHAM, SHAM, BH636_post1 and BH635_post2. The files start 63 to 68 min apart like every other rat's blocks (Methods D, ~62.5 min blocks), and every other sham rat has five blocks. The outcome depends on this choice; the label reading is shown as a variant.
The result holds under the repeated-measures reading of M3 only, which the criterion allows ("under one reading").

Assumed that each set of post hoc comparisons is its own Bonferroni family (reading i of M3), as Prism corrects each set of multiple comparisons it is asked for on its own; the paper names no family. Reading (ii) is shown. Under reading (ii) the comparison is not significant.

outcomes.statement: In the tFUS group, seizure count fell from baseline by 9%, 36% and 42% in the ipsilateral S1 and by 10%, 41% and 42% in the contralateral S1 during stimulation, post 1 and post 2, with significant reductions from baseline to post 1 and to post 2 in both hemispheres.
outcomes.quote: The Seizure Counts in the ipsilateral S1 decreased from baseline by 9%, 36%, and 42% for stimulation, post 1, and post 2, respectively. The decrease in Seizure Count recorded from the contralateral S1 showed slightly higher reduction rates of 10%, 41%, and 42% ... Both hemispheres displayed significant reductions in Seizure Count between baseline and post 1, as well as between baseline and post 2

statistics.about: baseline against post 1 and post 2, each hemisphere

outcomes.notes: Under reading (b) of M4 all six decreases are within tolerance. Reading (a) gives 24.1, 46.2, 49.4, 27.0, 47.2 and 50.3%, outside. Under the repeated-measures reading baseline against post 1 and post 2 are significant in both hemispheres (Bonferroni p = 0.016 and 0.0087 ipsilateral, 0.011 and 0.0059 contralateral, within family; 0.027, 0.014, 0.019 and 0.0098 over all ten). Under the ordinary reading none of the four is (p = 0.057 to 0.115).

outcomes.statement: Seizure count in the sham group stays steady, and the sham and tFUS groups differ significantly during post 1 and post 2.
outcomes.quote: Seizure Count within the sham group remained steady throughout, and there were significant differences between the sham and tFUS groups during post 1 and post 2
outcomes.notes: Sham against tFUS is significant at post 1 in both hemispheres under both readings, between family (ordinary p = 0.035 ipsilateral and 0.025 contralateral; repeated 0.040 and 0.029), and at post 2 in neither (ordinary 0.057 and 0.069; repeated 0.064 and 0.076). No sham block differs from sham baseline (p = 1). Only one of the two blocks is significant. With BH635 by its labels post 2 is significant (0.038 to 0.048) and post 1 is not (0.055 to 0.062), still one of the two.

outcomes.statement: In the tFUS group, percent time in seizure decreased significantly from baseline by 33% (ipsilateral) and 35% (contralateral) during stimulation and by 55% in post 1 and post 2 in both hemispheres.
outcomes.source: Results B, paragraph 2; Figure 3B; Discussion, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: The Percent Time in Seizure significantly decreased by 33% in the ipsilateral S1 and by 35% in the contralateral S1 for stimulation, 55% for post 1, and 55% for post 2 in both hemispheres, respectively
outcomes.notes: Reading (b) of M4 gives 32.5 and 34.8% at stimulation, 55.5 and 55.3% at post 1, 54.9 and 55.2% at post 2 (ipsilateral and contralateral; the measured values for the "each hemisphere" expectations are the ipsilateral ones), all within tolerance; reading (a) gives 35.8 to 57.3%, also within. Under the repeated-measures reading all six comparisons with baseline are significant (Bonferroni p from 0.0025 to below 0.0001); under the ordinary reading post 1 and post 2 are (0.008 to 0.012) and stimulation is not (0.22, 0.17).

outcomes.statement: In the sham group, percent time in seizure decreased slightly but did not differ significantly from baseline in any block.
outcomes.quote: Although Percent Time in Seizure for the sham condition decreased slightly across the experiment, there were no significant differences from baseline
outcomes.notes: The ANOVA readings disagree, and so do the family readings. Ordinary, no sham block differs from baseline (smallest Bonferroni p = 0.79). Repeated, contralateral post 2 differs in its family (p = 0.034; ipsilateral post 2 p = 0.062) and not over all ten comparisons (p = 0.057). Sham percent time falls from 24.0 to 16.4% (ipsilateral) and from 25.6 to 17.6% (contralateral). With BH635 by its labels contralateral post 2 is significant under the repeated reading (p = 0.024) and not under the ordinary one (p = 0.53).
deviations: Assumed that the paper's two-way ANOVA is the repeated-measures reading of M3, since the readings disagree on this claim of absence. Methods F says only "two-way ANOVA ... in GraphPad Prism"; the blocks are repeated on the same rats, and most of the paper's significant within-group changes of Fig. 3 (Results B; the count at post 1 and post 2, percent time at the stimulation block, the interval at contralateral post 1) are found only under the repeated-measures reading, while percent time at post 1 and post 2 is significant under both. Under the ordinary reading the claim would be reproduced.

Assumed that each set of post hoc comparisons is its own Bonferroni family (reading i of M3), as Prism corrects each set of multiple comparisons it is asked for on its own; the paper names no family. Reading (ii) is shown. Under reading (ii) the claim would be reproduced.

outcomes.statement: Percent time in seizure differs significantly between sham and tFUS during post 1 in the contralateral S1, and during stimulation and post 1 in the ipsilateral S1.
outcomes.quote: Comparing the sham and tFUS groups, there were significant differences during the post 1 session in the contralateral S1 and during the stimulation and post 1 sessions in the ipsilateral S1
outcomes.notes: tFUS is lower than sham in all three named comparisons (by 11.4, 9.8 and 10.0 percentage points), but none is significant. Contralateral post 1 p = 0.075 (ordinary) and 0.097 (repeated), ipsilateral stimulation 0.14 and 0.16, ipsilateral post 1 0.13 and 0.15, between family; larger over all ten comparisons.

outcomes.statement: Relative to baseline, the inter-seizure interval of the tFUS group increased by 27%, 49% and 28% (ipsilateral) and 30%, 52% and 31% (contralateral) during stimulation, post 1 and post 2; only post 1 in the contralateral S1 differed significantly from baseline.
outcomes.quote: Relative to baseline, the ipsilateral S1 Inter-Seizure Interval increased by 27%, 49%, and 28% during stimulation, post 1, and post 2 ... The contralateral S1 Inter-Seizure Interval increased by 30%, 52%, and 31% during stimulation, post 1, and post 2, respectively. Only the post 1 session in the contralateral S1 showed significant differences relative to baseline
outcomes.notes: Gap reading of the interval and reading (b) of M4, all six increases within tolerance. The two rats left out are BH634 and BH638 (no seizures at post 2). Under the repeated-measures reading contralateral post 1 is the only significant comparison with baseline under both family readings (p = 0.0086 within family, 0.014 over all ten; ipsilateral post 1 0.056 and 0.093, the others 0.69 or more). The ordinary reading finds none (contralateral post 1 p = 0.18). Onset-to-onset intervals give increases of 12.6 to 30.6%, outside tolerance.
deviations: Assumed that the Inter-Seizure Interval is the gap from one seizure's end to the next one's start. Methods C defines it as "time between neighboring seizures" and the claims file (M2) does not fix it; the onset-to-onset reading is shown. The gap reading gives the paper's six percentages to within 0.4 point.

outcomes.statement: The inter-seizure interval of the sham group stays steady, and sham and tFUS differ significantly during post 1 in both hemispheres.
outcomes.quote: The Inter-Seizure Interval of the sham group remained steady across the length of the experiment, and there were significant differences between sham and tFUS during post 1 in both hemispheres
outcomes.notes: Sham against tFUS at post 1 is significant in the contralateral S1 with tFUS higher (by 140 s; ordinary p = 0.027, repeated 0.037, between family) and not in the ipsilateral S1 (by 122 s; 0.051 and 0.061); the onset-to-onset interval gives the same (contralateral 0.029 and 0.038, ipsilateral 0.058 and 0.066). No sham block differs from sham baseline (p = 1). The claim holds in one hemisphere.

outcomes.statement: Seizure duration declines across time in both groups, and the only significant reduction is from baseline to post 2 in both hemispheres of the tFUS group.
outcomes.quote: The Seizure Duration showed a steady decline across time for both the sham group and the tFUS group ... however, the only significant reduction occurred from baseline to post 2 in both hemispheres of the tFUS group
outcomes.notes: Means decline in both groups (tFUS 59.8 to 48.7 s ipsilateral, 61.0 to 49.9 s contralateral; sham 53.0 to 37.8 and 56.8 to 40.6 s), but tFUS baseline against post 2 is not significant (Bonferroni p = 0.42 and 0.33 repeated, 0.62 and 0.59 ordinary), nor is any other within-group comparison (smallest p = 0.16). Counting the seizures within 2 s of either end of a block as cut off gives the same (0.42 and 0.33).
deviations: Per-rat mean durations, leaving out the 6 seizures that start at a block's first sample; the two tFUS rats without seizures at post 2 have no duration there (N = 8 at post 2).

outcomes.statement: There are no significant changes in theta, alpha or gamma power ratios in either hemisphere.
outcomes.quote: There were no significant changes in the theta, alpha, or gamma power ratios in either hemisphere
outcomes.notes: The M5 readings agree within each ANOVA reading; the ANOVA readings disagree. Ordinary, no within-group comparison against baseline is significant for theta, alpha or gamma. Repeated, the sham theta ratio rises above baseline in 4 or 5 of 12 comparisons under every M5 reading (ipsilateral post 2 p = 0.017 over the whole block, ratio 0.098 to 0.136; p = 0.0018 over the seizure periods, 0.078 to 0.131). Alpha and gamma have none. No between-group comparison is significant.
deviations: Assumed the repeated-measures reading of M3 is the paper's test, as for fig3b-sham-percent-time-no-change; under the ordinary reading the claim would be reproduced.
No ICA; which components the authors removed (Methods C) is not recorded. Common average reference and 60 Hz notch as in Methods C.

The channels are 8 (ipsilateral) and 25 (contralateral), the electrodes encircled in the drawing of Fig. S1, which prints the channel numbers; Methods E uses "the EEG electrode closest to the burr hole".
Seizure segment per hemisphere is the union of that hemisphere's labels; Welch PSD with 2 s Hann windows (the claims file's standard choice), periods shorter than a window skipped.

outcomes.statement: The beta power ratio of the tFUS group decreased significantly during stimulation and post 1 compared with baseline.
outcomes.source: Results C, paragraph 1; Figure 4C; Discussion, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: However, the beta ratio significantly decreased during tFUS and post 1 compared to baseline
outcomes.notes: Whole block, repeated-measures reading, the tFUS beta ratio at post 1 is significantly below baseline in both hemispheres (3-300 Hz total p = 0.0067 ipsilateral and 0.040 contralateral; 0 Hz to Nyquist 0.0019 and 0.018), but the condition block is not (p = 0.19 to 0.64) although its mean is lower (ipsilateral 0.445 to 0.417). Over the seizure periods the beta ratio does not fall (ipsilateral 0.493, 0.487, 0.500) and nothing is significant. Under the ordinary reading nothing is significant.
deviations: As for fig4-no-theta-alpha-gamma-power-change (no ICA, channels 8 and 25 from Fig. S1).

outcomes.statement: In the sham group, band power ratios show no significant change among time blocks or between hemispheres.
outcomes.quote: Within the sham group, the power ratios showed no significant change among time blocks or between hemispheres
outcomes.notes: Over the whole block beta has significant block and hemisphere effects under both readings (ordinary block p = 0.0004 and 0.0002 for the two totals, hemisphere p below 0.0001, 4 and 5 post hoc comparisons significant) and gamma a hemisphere effect (0.0037 and 0.0004). Over the seizure periods the repeated-measures reading finds a beta block effect (0.0030, 0.0025, 1 and 2 post hoc comparisons) and a gamma hemisphere effect (0.028, 0.013); the ordinary reading finds nothing in any band (smallest p = 0.09).
deviations: Under the ordinary reading the M5 readings disagree (whole block not reproduced, seizure periods reproduced), which the criterion would block as methods_underspecified; under the repeated-measures reading, assumed to be the paper's test as for fig3b-sham-percent-time-no-change, they agree.
As for fig4-no-theta-alpha-gamma-power-change (no ICA, channels 8 and 25 from Fig. S1).

outcomes.statement: The normalized asymmetry index of the tFUS group increases significantly relative to baseline in the theta and alpha bands, and differs significantly from the sham group in every band.
outcomes.quote: Normalized AI of the tFUS group increased significantly within the theta and alpha bands relative to baseline, and each frequency band displayed a significant difference between the normalized AI of the tFUS group and sham group

statistics.about: tFUS against baseline, theta and alpha

outcomes.notes: With AI on the band power (Eq. 1), mean baseline AI is negative in both groups (whole block, sham -0.58 to -0.61, tFUS -0.24 to -0.29). Whole block, repeated-measures reading, the tFUS AI rises above baseline, toward balance, in theta and alpha under both normalizations when a rising AI is read as a falling ratio under division (subtraction theta post 1 p = 0.0495, post 2 p = 0.010, alpha post 2 p = 0.012; division theta post 2 p = 0.0020, alpha post 2 p = 0.0005); read as the normalized value rising, only subtraction gives it. Sham against tFUS is not significant in any band, block or combination of readings. Over the seizure periods nothing is significant. With AI on band ratios the baseline AI is -0.09 to +0.04 and neither part holds, so the outcome would be not reproduced. Which quantity Eq. 1 is applied to is asked of the authors (findings); Methods E names "absolute power" by division and then the AI "for each of the aforementioned", which can be read either way.
deviations: Assumed that AI is computed on the band power (sum of PSD in the band) of channels 8 and 25, as Methods E says ("the relative difference in PSD between the ipsilateral and contralateral S1") and the Fig. 4 legend ("calculated using PSD values"), as for figs5-seizures-lower-ai; AI on the band over 3-300 Hz ratios is shown as a second reading, under which the outcome would be not reproduced. The seizure segment is the union of both hemispheres' labels.
"Increase" is shown in two readings, the normalized value rising and the AI rising; they differ under division when the baseline AI is negative. The outcome is the same under both.
As for fig4-no-theta-alpha-gamma-power-change (no ICA).

outcomes.statement: During seizures (baseline block, after 4-AP) the asymmetry index is negative and differs from zero in every band, more than in the pre-4-AP baseline state; seizures disrupt the normal interhemispheric balance.
outcomes.source: Discussion, paragraph 4; Figure S5; Results C, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: Our results indicated that seizures decreased AI, reflecting a disruption of normal interhemispheric balance

statistics.about: seizure AI against 0, each band (Fig. S5,
pre-4-AP baseline AI against 0, gamma (Fig. S5,
seizure against pre-4-AP baseline, alpha and beta (Fig. S5, *)

outcomes.notes: With AI on the band power, seizure AI of the baseline block is negative and below 0 in every band: -0.41 to -0.43 over the 16 rats (p < 0.0001), -0.27 to -0.30 over the 10 tFUS rats (p = 0.0001 to 0.0012), and the same over the 13 and 7 rats with a pre-4-AP recording (p < 0.0001; 0.004 to 0.014). It is lower than the pre-4-AP AI of the gaps between pulses in every band, for the 13 rats (difference -0.19 to -0.28; paired t p = 0.0006 or less; repeated-measures ANOVA p < 0.0001) and the 7 tFUS rats (paired 0.0003 to 0.022; repeated 0.018 or less); the whole recording gives the same. The ordinary ANOVA finds it in theta and alpha only for the 13 rats (0.028, 0.039; beta 0.095) and in no band for the 7. The pre-4-AP AI is itself negative (-0.17 to -0.26; below 0 in every band for the 13 rats, p = 0.0007 to 0.045; for the 7 tFUS rats only in gamma, p = 0.022). With AI on band ratios the seizure AI is -0.04 to +0.01, not below 0 in any band (p = 0.08 to 0.99), and the claim fails under every combination.
deviations: The pre-4-AP state is reading (b) of the claims file, the recording before the first injection. For 13 of the 16 rats (6 sham, 7 tFUS; not BH638, BH642, BH644) the EEG labelled "EEG data for PLV analysis" is the last recording before the first labelled block and ends 64 to 176 min before it, so before the monitoring block that the first injection opens (Fig. 1E). It carries a 20 ms tFUS pulse every 2 s (1 s in one file); assumed that the gaps between pulses, 250 ms after one onset to 20 ms before the next, stand for the pre-4-AP baseline, which the paper may have recorded without pulses. The whole recording is shown as a variant. Reading (a), the resting recording of the target confirmation, holds no EEG.

Assumed that AI is computed on the band power, as Methods E ("the relative difference in PSD") and the Fig. 4 legend ("calculated using PSD values") say; on the band over 3-300 Hz ratios the claim fails. Both are shown.
PSD of the gaps by a Hann periodogram of each gap, all cut to the shortest gap (1.73 s; 0.73 s in the 1 s file), averaged; a standard choice.

outcomes.statement: In epileptic rats, the S1 PLI of the tFUS group decreases in theta, alpha, beta and gamma bands during stimulation, post 1 and post 2 relative to baseline seizures, while non-S1 PLI does not decrease; the decrease of S1 connectivity is significant.
outcomes.quote: The S1 region of the tFUS group showed decreases in PLI within theta, alpha, beta, and gamma bands during stimulation, post 1, and post 2 compared to baseline. Comparatively, the non-S1 regions did not exhibit a reduction in PLI values due to stimulation
outcomes.notes: Per seizure and averaged, the tFUS S1 PLI is below the group's baseline in 8 of 12 band and block cells (theta and alpha at all three blocks; beta only at the condition block; gamma only at post 1); over concatenated samples 6 of 12. The non-S1 PLI falls too (not below baseline in only 4 of 12 cells under every reading), so that part fails. No sham against tFUS comparison of S1 PLI is significant under either ANOVA reading. The S1 decrease holds in two bands, the S1 specificity fails and the group difference fails; the criterion's partial clause names only the first and last of these, so the outcome is not reproduced (changed from partially reproduced after round 1).
deviations: S1 channels are 7, 8, 10, 12 and 21, 23, 25, 26, taken from the notes of the dandiset's PLV files; the paper draws them only in Fig. 5A, which the text read does not list.

Seizure periods are the union of both hemispheres' labels, 1 s or longer; the EEG is decimated by 3 to 1017 Hz before the band filters, a standard choice; band filters run on each seizure with 2 s of margin. No ICA.

outcomes.statement: Comparing seizures (baseline block) with the pre-4-AP baseline state, the PLI change of S1 pairs differs significantly from that of non-S1 pairs in every band; the paper says PLI differences between wild-type and seizure rats may reflect distinct baseline network states.
outcomes.quote: The PLI differences between wild-type and seizure rats may reflect distinct baseline network states

statistics.about: theta, seizure S1 against seizure non-S1 (read from the Fig. S7B marks)
alpha, beta and gamma, seizure S1 against seizure non-S1 (read from the Fig. S7B marks)

outcomes.notes: With the pre-4-AP state from the gaps between pulses of the PLV recording (13 rats), the seizure PLI of the baseline block is 2 to 5 times the pre-4-AP PLI in both regions (concatenated, S1 0.10 to 0.24 against 0.03 to 0.08). The S1 change exceeds the non-S1 change in every band (difference reading, by 0.006 to 0.087), significantly only in theta over concatenated samples under every ANOVA and rat reading (13 rats p = 0.0067 ordinary, 0.0004 repeated; 7 tFUS rats 0.024, 0.026) and in theta and gamma per seizure under the repeated reading for the 13 rats (0.0017, 0.044). Alpha and beta are never significant and the ratio reading finds nothing. Unlike Fig. S7B, where seizure non-S1 is below zero, both changes are positive.
deviations: The pre-4-AP state is the gaps between pulses of the PLV recording, as for figs5-seizures-lower-ai (13 of 16 rats; an assumption). Its PLI is taken over the concatenated gap samples; the per-gap PLI (gaps of 1.7 s) is 1.7 to 4 times higher, the short-window bias, and is shown only.
S1 channels and seizure periods as for fig6-epileptic-pli-s1-decrease.

outcomes.statement: tFUS of the CC in wild-type rats evokes potentials in the left S1 LFP that differ significantly from the sham (resting) recording at some time points.
outcomes.source: Figure 5B; Methods D, paragraph 1; Results D, paragraph 1
outcomes.inferred: Read from the Fig. 5B legend ("Yellow shadings denote significant differences between the tFUS and sham groups") and the Results' "From EPs induced by CC tFUS"; no sentence states which time points differ.
outcomes.notes: The readings disagree. With the mean over the 64 channels, 2 of 18 combinations of position (CENTER, largest EP, largest EP chosen on odd trials and tested on even trials), sham onsets (every 2 s, random, the file's own intervals) and ANOVA (ordinary, repeated) find significant time points, both CENTER with random onsets (ordinary 13 of 610 points from 66.5 ms, smallest Bonferroni p = 0.013; repeated 26 points from 64.2 ms, p = 0.00067); the other 16 find none (smallest p = 0.054 to 1). With each channel, 1 to 55 of 64 channels have a significant point depending on the combination. The CENTER channel-mean EP reaches 3.1 uV, the sham 1.7 uV. The interval starts are the burst onsets: 1.4-1.5 kHz power, the band of the 1.5 kHz pulse repetition frequency, peaks 10 to 60 ms after them in 13 of 23 CENTER recordings and in none of the 23 resting ones, and the LFP shows no clear response at any lag of the 2 s cycle. The criterion blocks the claim when the readings disagree. Question for the authors (findings) which channels, which position and which sham onsets were used.
deviations: The repeated-measures reading of the time-point test adds a random intercept per rat to the group by time point two-way ANOVA (pooled error); the first version used a paired t-test per time point, which the claims-file check had replaced with this ANOVA.
The largest-EP position reading picks the position on the data it tests; a split-half variant picks it on the odd trials and tests the even trials.

outcomes.statement: In wild-type rats, gamma band PLI decreases during and after tFUS relative to the pre-tFUS window in most brain regions, on average in both S1 and non-S1 regions, while it increases slightly in the sham.
outcomes.quote: the PLI of the gamma band decreased during and after tFUS in most brain regions ... whereas the gamma PLI increased slightly in the sham group ... On average, the gamma PLI of the tFUS group decreased in both the S1 and non-S1 regions relative to the pre-tFUS window
outcomes.notes: The sham, the EEG of the resting baseline recording of the target confirmation, is not in the dandiset; its resting recordings hold only the intracranial LFP. The tFUS part, from the PLV EEG files of 20 rats, does not hold once the windows have equal length. Per trial, the PLI equals its trial-shuffled floor in every window (gamma S1 0.625 pre, 0.613 tFUS, 0.630 post; floors 0.628, 0.615, 0.629). Over concatenated samples the gamma PLI changes by S1 +0.002 and non-S1 +0.005 in the 0 to 20 ms window and -0.008 and -0.002 after it, with 47% of pairs decreasing in each. The decreases of the first version (20 to 200 ms window, 100% of pairs per trial) were the bias of comparing 549 samples with 61.
deviations: The 20 to 200 ms window is compared with the 20 ms pre window through the mean PLI of its nine 20 ms sub-windows, since a PLI over fewer samples is biased upwards; the whole window is shown. Each PLI is given with a noise floor, the contralateral channels taken from the next trial.

outcomes.statement: In wild-type rats, theta, alpha and beta PLI decrease only within the S1 regions during tFUS.
outcomes.source: Results D, paragraph 1; Figure 5G-I; Figure S6
outcomes.quote: The PLI in theta, alpha, and beta bands only decreased within the S1 regions during the tFUS conditions
outcomes.notes: In no band and under no combination of readings does the S1 PLI fall while the non-S1 PLI does not, with equal-length windows or with the whole 20 to 200 ms window. In the 0 to 20 ms window S1 PLI is not below pre in theta, alpha or beta under any reading (differences +0.0002 to +0.070). After it, over concatenated 20 ms sub-windows, both regions fall slightly in alpha (S1 -0.010, non-S1 -0.014) and beta (-0.016, -0.026). The per-trial PLI is at its trial-shuffled floor (theta S1 0.976 pre, floor 0.976), and the concatenated PLI (0.10 to 0.20) is about 0.02 above its floor. The outcome rests on the PLV recordings standing for the target-confirmation EEG; with the claims file's data, which the dandiset lacks, the claim would be blocked (data_missing) like fig5cdj-wild-type-gamma-pli-decrease. Which recordings the PLI was computed on is asked of the authors (findings).
deviations: Assumed that the epochs are the first 200 pulses of the dandiset's PLV EEG files (20 ms pulses, labelled EEG data for PLV analysis), for 20 of the 23 rats; the claims file reads them as the 200 bursts of the target confirmation, whose EEG is not in the dandiset. The Methods' "tFUS (20 ms of stimulation" fits these files, and they are the only wild-type EEG with pulses that the dandiset holds.
S1 channels from the PLV files' notes (see fig6-epileptic-pli-s1-decrease). The ratio reading divides the region's mean PLI by its mean pre PLI, a standard choice.
Equal-length windows (nine 20 ms sub-windows of 20 to 200 ms) and trial-shuffled noise floors, as for fig5cdj-wild-type-gamma-pli-decrease.

findings.statement: The seizure label table (intervals/custom_intervals_table_name) of all 70 labelled EEG blocks gives start and stop times in minutes, while NWB prescribes seconds; the stops reach 62.7 in blocks of 3750 s. Read as minutes the labels match the EEG (30 to 80 Hz power 2.5 to 50 times higher inside them in all 136 block-hemispheres); read as seconds they do not. The EP and PLV files' interval tables are in seconds.

The five block files of sham rat BH635 are labelled BASELINE, SHAM, SHAM, BH636_post1 (another rat's number) and BH635_post2, with no post3, while every other sham rat has BASELINE, SHAM, post1, post2, post3. The files follow each other at 63 to 68 min like the other rats' blocks. BH649's post 3 file has the session id None in its path.
Every file gives the subject as "HSD:WI rat" (Envigo's Wistar code) of age P24W, while the paper used Sprague-Dawley rats (Envigo) of 3 to 6 months.

The ElectricalSeries of the EP files is described as "EEG data" though the files hold the 64 intracranial channels of left S1 (location Left S1, notes "LFP signal for EP test"). The PLV files are labelled 1Hz but 19 of 20 carry their pulses every 2 s.

The files do not say which EEG channels were used to label the seizures (channels 8 and 25, read from the drawing of Fig. S1) or which channels cover S1 (given only in the notes of the PLV files, not in the electrode tables of the labelled blocks).

The target-confirmation recordings do not say which transducer position was chosen for the experiment ("the coordinates with the clearest EP", supplement), so the tFUS EPs of Fig. 5B cannot be selected.

The EEG of the resting baseline of the target confirmation (the sham of Figs. 5E-F) is not in the dandiset; the resting recordings hold only the intracranial LFP, and the first monitoring block after the first injection was not deposited. The EEG before the first 4-AP injection (Figs. S5 and S7) is there only as the PLV recordings, which carry tFUS pulses and are not described as pre-4-AP recordings; 13 of the 16 epileptic rats have one. PLV EEG files exist for 20 of the 23 wild-type rats (not BH638, BH642, BH644), while Fig. 5 gives N = 23.

Question for the authors. Was the two-way ANOVA of Figs. 2 to 4 and 6 ordinary or repeated measures (or Prism's mixed-effects model), and which comparisons formed each Bonferroni family? Most of the paper's within-group significance in Fig. 3 appears here only under a repeated-measures reading; this attempt assumed repeated measures, and each set of comparisons as its own family, for the claims where the readings disagree.

Question for the authors. For Fig. 5B, which LFP channel or channels, which target-confirmation recording, which sham onsets in the resting recording and what time resolution were tested? Under the readings tried here the result ranges from no significant time point to 13 of 610 points from 66.5 ms.

Question for the authors. Over which segment were band power, AI and seizure PLI computed (whole block or seizure periods, and for two hemispheres whose labels differ, which periods), what total was the band power divided by, was Eq. 1 applied to the band power or to the band ratio, and was AI normalized to the group's baseline by division or by subtraction? With a negative baseline AI the two normalizations give opposite directions; on band ratios fig4ef-ai-increase and figs5-seizures-lower-ai would not be reproduced, on band power (assumed here) they are partly and fully reproduced.

Question for the authors. Was the wild-type PLI of Fig. 5 computed on EEG recorded during the 67 ms bursts of the target confirmation, or on the separate recordings with 20 ms pulses that the dandiset labels EEG data for PLV analysis? This attempt assumed the latter for fig5ghi-low-band-pli-s1-only, since only those are in the dandiset.

Methods E gives the wild-type tFUS window as "20 ms of stimulation" of "200 EPs from the target confirmation procedure", but the target-confirmation bursts last 67 ms (supplement). The dandiset resolves it with separate EEG recordings of 20 ms pulses made in the wild-type phase, labelled EEG data for PLV analysis, which the paper does not describe.

The baseline AI of the labelling channels on band power is strongly negative in both groups (whole block, sham -0.58 to -0.61, tFUS -0.24 to -0.29), and negative before 4-AP too (-0.17 to -0.26), so the contralateral channel carries 1.7 to 4 times the ipsilateral power; on band over total ratios the AI is near 0. The asymmetry is in the total power of channels 8 and 25. The paper reports only AI normalized to the baseline.

In the target-confirmation LFP the trial-mean response shows no clear evoked potential at any lag of the 2 s cycle, at the CENTER position as in the resting recording (mean RMS over channels 5.2 uV from 0 to 200 ms against 6.8 uV later in the cycle), although 1.4-1.5 kHz power, the pulse repetition frequency, marks the bursts at the interval starts in 13 of 23 CENTER recordings.

The PLV EEG recordings of the epileptic rats, which 13 of the 16 have, are the last recordings before the first 4-AP injection (they end 64 to 176 min before the baseline block), but nothing in the files says so, and the timeline of Fig. 1E does not list them.

verifications.reviewed: Round 1. The first executed notebooks with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper module and the claims file, with the paper. The verifier tested helper functions on synthetic inputs and queried the archive's asset metadata. Its report had no attempt record and gave its own outcome for each claim; 19 of 22 agree with the record as it then was.

disagreements.reason: Sham against tFUS at post 1 is significant in both hemispheres under ordinary ANOVA (0.035, 0.025), and sham is steady. Post 2 reaches p<0.05 only in the repeated reading (ipsilateral 0.0458), and that rests on a z reference (problem 1); the ordinary reading has the same statistic and gives p=0.057 (cells 23, 25).

Contralateral post 1 is significant under both ANOVAs (0.027 ordinary), with tFUS higher. Ipsilateral reaches 0.0385 only through the z reference (ordinary 0.0508, same statistic). No sham block differs from baseline (cell 36).
tFUS S1 is below baseline in only 8 (or 6) of 12 cells. Non-S1 is also below in 8 of 12. Sham S1 falls as much or more. No S1 sham against tFUS comparison is significant (cells 22–23).

The full executed notebooks of the first revision with their conclusion cells and summaries, the README, the helper module, the claims file and this record, with the paper. The verifier could not run the module (no numpy in its environment) and checked the code and the outputs. It agreed with all 22 outcomes. Of its round-1 points, all nine are resolved, point 3 (EP alignment) mostly. What it lists as remaining is the protocol's absence rule, which it cannot check and on which fig3b-sham-percent-time-no-change, fig4-no-theta-alpha-gamma-power-change and figs4-sham-power-no-change rest through the repeated-measures reading, the two missing flags, and family (i), on which fig2f-sham-percent-time-post3 and fig3b-sham-percent-time-no-change turn. entries.name: 001683-gao-2026
entries.title: White-matter tFUS against 4-AP seizures in rats (Gao et al. 2026)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Gao, Frake, Durand and He (2026) on dandiset 001683, which holds the EEG and seizure labels of 16 rats with 4-AP seizures (10 given focused ultrasound to the corpus callosum, 6 sham) and the evoked-potential and EEG recordings of the wild-type phase of 23 rats. It compares seizure count, percent time in seizure, interval and duration between groups and time blocks, band power, the asymmetry index and the phase lag index, and the evoked potentials.
